blueprint.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

item.vignette: A 14-year-old boy has slowly progressive distal leg weakness, frequent ankle sprains, and numbness of the feet. Examination shows pes cavus, calf muscle atrophy, absent ankle reflexes, and reduced distal vibration sensation. His father has similar findings. Nerve-conduction studies show uniformly slowed conduction velocities. Genetic testing demonstrates a duplication that includes PMP22 on chromosome 17.
item.lead_in: Which cellular abnormality most directly accounts for the slowed nerve conduction?

options.A: Loss of anterior horn motor neurons due to reduced SMN protein
options.B: Excess PMP22 disrupting Schwann-cell myelin formation and maintenance
options.C: Accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids from defective peroxisomal import
options.D: Reduced frataxin causing mitochondrial dysfunction in sensory neurons
options.E: Loss of maternal UBE3A expression in neurons

item.tested_construct: Cellular mechanism of CMT1A demyelinating neuropathy

explanation.key_explanation: CMT1A is most commonly caused by duplication of PMP22. Excess PMP22 disrupts Schwann-cell myelin formation and maintenance, producing a demyelinating peripheral neuropathy with uniformly slowed nerve-conduction velocities.

distractor_explanations.A: SMN deficiency causes lower motor-neuron loss in spinal muscular atrophy rather than a length-dependent demyelinating sensory-motor neuropathy.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. PMP22 duplication causes Schwann-cell myelin dysfunction and slowed peripheral nerve conduction.
distractor_explanations.C: ABCD1 deficiency causes peroxisomal VLCFA accumulation with cerebral myelin and adrenal involvement.
distractor_explanations.D: Frataxin deficiency causes Friedreich ataxia and does not explain the PMP22 duplication.
distractor_explanations.E: Maternal UBE3A loss causes Angelman syndrome, not inherited demyelinating neuropathy.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect PMP22 duplication in CMT1A with excess PMP22 in Schwann cells, impaired peripheral myelin formation/maintenance, and uniformly slowed conduction velocity.

evidence_map.claim: SMN1 deficiency causes spinal muscular atrophy through motor-neuron loss.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not fit sensory loss plus PMP22 duplication and demyelinating conduction pattern.

evidence_map.claim: PMP22 duplication increases PMP22 and disrupts Schwann-cell myelin formation and maintenance in CMT1A.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Directly explains uniform slowing of conduction.

evidence_map.claim: ABCD1 deficiency impairs peroxisomal VLCFA transport and causes X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Different organelle and phenotype from CMT1A.

evidence_map.claim: FXN GAA expansion reduces frataxin and causes Friedreich ataxia.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not explain the provided PMP22 duplication.

evidence_map.claim: Loss of maternal UBE3A function in neurons causes Angelman syndrome.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not cause this autosomal-dominant demyelinating neuropathy.

sources.title: PMP22 gene: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: PMP22 duplication causes excess PMP22, disrupting Schwann-cell myelin formation and maintenance; deletion reduces PMP22 and causes pressure-palsy neuropathy.

sources.title: Spinal muscular atrophy: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: SMN1 mutations cause SMA; SMN2 copy number modifies severity because additional SMN2 copies produce more functional SMN protein.

sources.title: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: ABCD1 encodes ALDP, which transports very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes; deficiency disrupts VLCFA breakdown and causes accumulation toxic to myelin and adrenal cortex.

sources.title: Friedreich ataxia: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: FXN GAA repeat expansion reduces frataxin production; frataxin is important for normal mitochondrial function.

sources.title: Angelman syndrome: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: In CNS neurons, the maternal UBE3A copy is active; loss of maternal UBE3A function causes Angelman syndrome.
